extracted.intended_audience: research teams and principal investigators preparing proposals to IARPA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria used to evaluate research proposals submitted to IARPA, emphasizing high‑risk/high‑payoff projects and judged against scientific merit, programmatic relevance, cost realism, team capability, and test & evaluation plans. Uses the Heilmeier Catechism and agency process features (independent T&E, multiple performers, open research, phase‑gated structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: What are you trying to do?
rubrics_metrics.description: What are you trying to do?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Heilmeier Catechism. Define the project objectives clearly and without jargon so reviewers immediately understand the proposed goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: How is it done today, and what are the limits of current practice?
rubrics_metrics.description: How is it done today, and what are the limits of current practice?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Heilmeier Catechism. Explain current state‑of‑the‑art approaches and their limitations to motivate the need for the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: What's new in your approach and why do you think it will be successful?
rubrics_metrics.description: What's new in your approach and why do you think it will be successful?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Heilmeier Catechism. Emphasize novelty, the mechanism by which success will be achieved, and evidence or reasoning supporting feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who cares?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Heilmeier Catechism. State the stakeholders or consumers of the capability and articulate why the intelligence community (or other stakeholders) would value the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you're successful, what difference will it make?
rubrics_metrics.description: If you're successful, what difference will it make?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Heilmeier Catechism. Describe concrete impact and how success translates into actionable advantage or capability for the IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are the risks?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Heilmeier Catechism. Identify technical, schedule, and integration risks and, where possible, mitigation strategies or contingency plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much will it cost?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Heilmeier Catechism. Provide realistic, justified cost estimates and link budget items to planned activities and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: How long will it take?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Heilmeier Catechism. Provide a clear timeline, phase durations, and criteria for go/no‑go decisions; align schedule with planned demonstrations and evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and Technical Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation and approach; likelihood of meeting metrics; soundness of methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators assess novelty of the approach, whether the methodology is rigorous and appropriate, and the plausibility that the project will meet the program's quantitative metrics. Provide robust technical rationale, preliminary results when available, and clear links between methods and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct relevance to BAA topic; contribution to IARPA mission; impact on intelligence community problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate alignment with the specific BAA topic and overall IARPA objectives. Explain how outcomes address concrete IC needs or problems and why IARPA is the appropriate sponsor versus other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonableness of proposed budget; cost‑benefit analysis; resource allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgets should be realistic and justified. Reviewers consider whether proposed costs are appropriate for the planned work, whether resources are allocated efficiently, and whether expected benefits justify expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team Capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Past performance; expertise of proposed team; available facilities and infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the PI and team qualifications, track record on related work, and whether institutional resources/facilities support successful execution. Include evidence of relevant prior accomplishments and complementary expertise across team members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test and Evaluation Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantifiable milestones; metrics that can be independently verified; realistic phase planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a detailed, measurable T&E plan with milestones tied to quantitative metrics. Ensure metrics are independently verifiable (IARPA uses an independent T&E team) and that phase planning supports objective go/no‑go assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Test and Evaluation (T&E)
rubrics_metrics.description: IARPA has an independent testing and evaluation (T&E) team that confirms the results reported by the performers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments, metrics, and reporting so results can be replicated and validated by an independent T&E team. Avoid unverifiable claims; include data formats, baselines, and procedures necessary for third‑party verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple Performers per Goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs normally have multiple performers addressing each technical goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IARPA favors multiple concurrent approaches. Proposals should justify why the team's approach is competitive and complementary, and be prepared for head‑to‑head comparisons. Emphasize differentiators and potential advantages in comparative testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Research Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Majority of projects are conducted through open, unclassified research; performers encouraged to publish results in open, peer‑reviewed literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, structure work to allow open publication and community scrutiny. Prepare for release of non‑sensitive results and describe plans for dissemination (papers, datasets) while noting any classified needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel members are required to declare potential conflicts of interest and sign non‑disclosure agreements prior to access to technical proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect strict COI handling. Do not assume panelists will see proprietary context beyond NDAs; structure proposal to be reviewable under these constraints and avoid unnecessary proprietary barriers to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission emphasis: high‑risk, high‑payoff research
rubrics_metrics.description: IARPA invests in high‑risk, high‑payoff research that can provide the United States with overwhelming intelligence advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target ambitious, potentially transformational advances rather than incremental improvements. Clearly articulate the magnitude of potential payoff and link high risk to commensurate potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical Program Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi‑phase (Phase 1, 2, optional Phase 3); phase‑gated with go/no‑go milestones; quarterly progress reports; major reviews at phase boundaries; final demonstration with measurable outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan proposals around multi‑phase execution with clear deliverables and gate criteria. Provide phase schedules, measurable demo criteria, and a reporting plan for quarterly updates and review readiness at phase boundaries.
